newsitem.title: CHILE: Chileans dam river to avoid stink at summit.
newsitem.headline: Chileans dam river to avoid stink at summit.

text.p: Chilean officials said on Wednesday they had dammed a stinking river to stop it marring a 21-nation summit next week.

Officials erected a temporary dyke on the Marga Marga river, which meanders through the city of Vina del Mar, to prevent foul-smelling material flowing downstream to where the Ibero-American Summit starts on Monday, city officials said.
''It's a temporary dam. This way, there will be less material in the river to cause a bad odour,'' city administrator Juan Cristobal Bonnefoy said.

The dyke, erected about a mile (two km) upstream from where the presidents meet, will allow water to pass but will trap noxious organic material which can make the Marga Marga smell bad at this time of year, Bonnefoy told Reuters.

The leaders of 19 Latin American countries, the prime ministers of Spain and Portugal and the King of Spain will open the summit in Santiago on Sunday and then move to Vina de Mar on Monday for more meetings and the summit's closure.
Summit organisers have been cleaning up both cities for the meeting.
